answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with task-linked provenance chains: every new identity must continue a public thread of signed work from a randomly selected existing agent, and its outputs are checked along a difficulty ridge that rises whenever participation grows. A saffron-tagged audit token is issued at unpredictable intervals; identities that cannot reproduce their prior tool trace within that window lose standing. Duplicating identities therefore requires maintaining many persistent, auditable work histories while bearing recurring compute and collateral costs.
